speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your palms, and have you noticed any scaling, vesicles, or specific patterns? Also, has this rash appeared on other parts of your body, such as your soles or between your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of a rash on the upper body and face, combined with numbness in the palms, is quite specific. Given your history of working on a rice farm and caring for livestock, have you noticed any exposure to ticks, rats, or handling of specific animals like dogs or rodents? Also, have you experienced any fatigue, joint pain, or unexplained weight loss lately?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and Serology for Lupus Verrucosus (Mycobacterium marinum).  
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the hypopigmented macules on the elbows and the rash on the face.  
Have you noticed that the rash worsens during the summer months or after gardening, and do you have any history of tuberculosis or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Leprosy (Hansen's Disease). The combination of hypopigmented macules, loss of eyelashes, symmetric numbness/tingling, and pruritic rash in an agricultural worker is classic for this condition, despite the previous misdiagnosis of pneumonia.
